text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- The Finnish economy is not at risk of overheating, mainly due to massive unemployment, economists say.
- Taxes in Finland can be paid in euros from 1999 if EMU starts as planned, finance ministry says. It is due to release a euro change-over plan today.
- Unions agreed on equalising pension ages for men and women, and the Confederation of Salaried Employees in Finland (STTK) withdrew strike plans.
- Former Russian ambassador to Finland and adviser to President Boris Yeltsin Jurij Derjabin says in his memoirs he backed Yeltsin's reported warning against Finnish NATO membership.
- EU food aid divided students; northern aid packages ran out while southern cities were left with a surplus.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Decisions to join EMU and constitutional changes replacing the markka with the euro should be made simultaneously, says opposition leader Esko Aho.
- Alcohol sales and taxation should be liberalised sooner than by 2003 to avoid a crash, says wine and liquor factory Marli's managing director Heikki Elo.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Construction costs will rise gradually in the near moths, industry experts say.
- Sweden's stance on EMU will have a vast impact on Finland's decisions, opposition leader Esko Aho says.
- Mutual euro conversion rates for EMU-countries should be based on current ERM central parity rates, says French EMU expert, professor Charles Wyplosz visiting Helsinki.

- Strong competitiveness has helped Finland's chemical industry benefit from economic upturn better than its European Union counterparts, says Neste president Jaakko Ihamuotila who chairs the industry lobby in Finland.
AAMULEHTI
- Finns are increasingly confident in the future and believe politicians and other public actors are more seriously countering unemployment than a year ago, a Suomen Gallup poll shows.
- The weather will stay cold until midsummer, says forecaster Antti-Juhani Leino who uses old Finnish traditional methods.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Finnish architect Kristian Gullichsen won an international competition in Spain on a new cultural centre and library for the university in Lerida.
- Unemployment costs Helsinki about one billion markka a year, and the City agreed with the unemployment office on a campaign against joblessness.
